text: Power BI's dashboard applies one flat ninety-day rule to every customer equally. This lesson adds something Power BI's visuals aren't built for, comparing each customer against their own buying rhythm.

Pull order history with pandas, then compute each customer's own gap between consecutive orders, their personal average and standard deviation, requiring at least four prior gaps for a meaningful baseline.

Compare each customer's current gap since their last order to their own baseline with a z-score, and flag anyone above two who's still inside the ninety-day active window. A monthly regular whose gap suddenly stretches to forty-five days against a personal average of twenty-eight is exactly the case this is built to catch, and exactly the case invisible to the flat ninety-day rule.
Export the flagged list as its own watchlist, deliberately not a new Power BI measure. Folding it into the churn rate would quietly change the agreed definition without anyone approving that change.
A complementary early-warning signal, not a replacement for the agreed metric. Next: rebuilding the same core view in Tableau, for the field team's own tool.
